title: Resource is not removed
body:
Folks, we've found a problem that when you remove a resource, it stills continue to be listed as published. For instance:

```resourceManager.removeResource(name);```

Even if you call that twice, it remains available. Please, it is a bug or are we doing something wrong here? 

Thanks in advance!
author: orpiske

comments.body:
@orpiske, I moved it to quarkus-mcp-server. 

Do you have a reproducer maybe?
@orpiske I think `ResourceManager#removeResource(String)` accepts the `uri`, not the `name` and the method should return the removed resource in case of successful removal.

Thanks guys 🙏  

The issue was on our end: we were removing by name instead of by URI. After adjusting the code, it worked nicely!

> Thanks guys 🙏
> 
> The issue was on our end: we were removing by name instead of by URI. After adjusting the code, it worked nicely!

Yep, it's a bit confusing. But we decided to follow the spec where a resource is always identified by a `uri`, e.g. in a `resources/read` request.

I'm glad it works now. Let us know if you find something else...

title: Programmatic API do add resources, prompts, tools, etc.
author: mkouba

comments.body: FYI @orpiske ... I will add some docs tomorrow.
That is awesome @mkouba !!!
@maxandersen FYI `@WrapBusinessError` can be declared on a method or on a class. And it wraps all exceptions by default. I'm not so sure about the name but did not find anything better.
How about @WrapOnException ? wether its business or internal is separate concern i feel?

> How about @WrapOnException ? wether its business or internal is separate concern i feel?

Hm, I don't like that. The point is to wrap an exception if it represents a business error. If it doesn't then we don't wrap but log an exception and reply "internal error" to the client.

title: Using programmatically
body:
Hey folks, I'm considering using the Quarkus MCP server for an idea, but I must do so programmatically (i.e.: I cannot use the annotations, as most of the tools, resources, etc need to be defined at runtime). 

Please, do you have any pointers as to how someone could get started with that using the Quarkus MCP server?
author: orpiske

comments.body: We don't have an API for this yet. It's on the roadmap though.

@orpiske can you explain what your use case is that results in you needing a programmatic API for registering the various components?

Thanks

my usecase is abilty to point to have a MCP server that is given an openAI endpoint and exposes all or part of that API in mcp tools.

could do that at build time too but then I would need a binary per every version of the api.
Essentially, I would like to define things in runtime ... to add and remove resources at will, for instance.
